short: The last non-Christian emperor, a scholar-soldier whose brief, energetic reign ended on a failed Persian campaign.
full:
Julian, a cousin of Constantius II raised in near-isolation after a purge of his family, was sent to govern Gaul as Caesar in 355 CE and proved an unexpectedly capable general, defeating a Germanic confederation at Strasbourg in 357 CE. His troops proclaimed him Augustus in 360 CE when Constantius tried to redeploy them east, and he became sole emperor without a fight when Constantius died on 3 November 361 CE.

Julian used his brief reign to trim the imperial bureaucracy, reduce taxes, and reverse decades of state favour toward Christianity, earning later Christian writers' epithet "the Apostate." He invaded Sasanian Persia in 363 CE, won an early battle near Ctesiphon but could not take the city, and was killed by a spear during the difficult retreat on 26 June 363 CE, leaving no heir and ending the Constantinian dynasty.
